title: Mass Shootings and Their Impact on Retail
eligible_reason: Store-month panel of retail establishments near mass-shooting incidents with matched control stores. Treatment D = treat x post switches on at the incident month, which varies across 486 incidents (18 monthly adoption cohorts, G = 7..24, i.e., 2022-01 to 2023-06); matched control stores are never treated (G = 0). Main Table 2 and Table 3 columns 3-5 are static TWFE regressions with store and year-month FE, no controls, clustered on cluster_key; Figure 2 is an unstacked relative-month event study with fixest i(rel_time2, treat, ref = -1). The authors reference a Callaway-Sant'Anna att_gt estimate in the code.
design_notes: Data: masked_data_main.parquet (493,020 store-months; 16,434 stores, 3,323 treated within 0.25 mi; 30 months 2021-07..2023-12; 486 incidents), masked_data_foot.parquet (foot traffic, 376,170 rows, 12,539 stores, 2,242 treated), masked_data_2mi.parquet (stores up to 2 mi, 2.79M rows, 76,626 stores, 29,096 treated). Matching lists placekey_match_main.csv (16,620 treated-control pairs) and placekey_match_2mi.csv. Variables: treat, post, D = treat*post, G (first treated month, 0 for controls), time (1-30), placekey (anonymized store id), id (numeric), cluster_key (13,597 distinct keys in main file; README calls it an incident-level key but it has more levels than Incident.ID), naics_code/naics4, distance_1mi, consecutive_zero_spend, close. slice_data() keeps treated stores satisfying the indicator and all their matched controls; expand = FALSE so controls matched to several treated stores enter once. Table 2 sample = treated stores with max consecutive zero-spend months <= 2 ('operating'). Figure 2 sample further requires >= 12 months pre and post for treated stores; rel_time2 binned at +/-12. CS att_gt (did package, est_method = 'dr', base_period = 'universal', aggte 'simple') is shown as a commented example in the Rmd and described as 'one of the Callaway and Sant'Anna DID result[s]'.
estimators_reported: callaway_santanna (did::att_gt; referenced in code, location in paper unverified)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: G takes 18 distinct treated values (7..24 = 2022-01..2023-06) in the main and foot-traffic files; controls have G = 0.
modern_estimators_named: callaway_santanna (did::att_gt, doubly robust, universal base period, simple aggregation) - referenced in code.Rmd lines 123-142

data_files_note: README: 'Due to a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) restriction, we offer a de-identified synthetic dataset by masking the original dataset. Consequently, the coefficients using this noisy version of the dataset are generally attenuated compared to those published in the paper.' All three parquet files and both matching csv files needed by code.Rmd are present; code runs end-to-end on them.
software_note: R: fixest (feols, i(), iplot, etable), arrow, tidyverse, stargazer; did package for the commented CS example; code in an R Markdown file (code.Rmd) plus result_functions.R
screener_notes: Design is clean (binary absorbing treatment, many monthly cohorts, never-treated matched controls, TWFE without controls, cluster-robust SEs, event study with ref = -1), and TWFE/CSA/BJS can all be run directly on the shipped files using placekey/id, time, G and D. The constraint is that the shipped data are masked/synthetic by the authors' own description, so replicated numbers will not match the published tables; treat as 'approximate' replication at best unless the original data can be obtained. Table/column mapping follows the Rmd section headers (Table 1 descriptives, Table 2 Panels A-B, Figure 2, Table A2/Figure 3, Table 3). Published coefficients unknown (no article text); the Rmd comments only give the economic-cost figures (211,410 average loss per store; ~27bn aggregate).
